newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil strengthens on futures, cargoes quiet.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil strengthens on futures, cargoes quiet.

text.p: NWE gas oil strengthened on Wednesday with higher benchmark IPE futures, although traders said the cargo market was fairly quiet.
The October IPE contract closed $4 up $218.50 a tonne.

Traders said buyers were holding out for lower premiums on the expectation that the arrival of some 400,000 tonnes of north American gas oil in Europe at the beginning of October will pressure them down.
"A lot of buyers are hoping the U.S. cargoes will bring the market off, but it's still unclear how many of the 10 to 11 cargoes have already been placed," one trader said.
Russian premiums were wide apart at Oct IPE +$5.50/+$7 cif Hamburg. "Both sides are being stubborn," a broker said.
A small parcel of low sulphur was reported done into Hamburg at Oct +$18, but traders said prices on larger cargoes were closer to Oct +$16.50 to +$17.

On the barge market, premiums eased slightly to Oct +$8/+$10 in later trade as futures strengthened. Traders said most demand was out of Belgium were people were stocking up ahead of expected increases in excise duty.
